title: $\varrho$: The Self-Referential Fixed Point of the Complex Exponential
summary: I was taught that $e^x = x$ has no solution, and taught to leave it at that. But in mathematics "no solution" has usually meant "not on this line yet": $x^2 = -1$ waited for the complex plane, and $e^x = x$ turns out to be waiting there too. Over $\mathbb{C}$ the exponential has a fixed point $\varrho = 0.318\ldots + 1.337\ldots\,i$, the unique solution of $\exp(z) = z$ in the strip $0 < \operatorname{Im} z < π$ (equivalently $-W_{-1}(-1)$), and it carries more structure than its one-line definition lets on. At $\varrho$ the rectangular and log-polar coordinates of a complex number coincide,…
